slides.title: The Break Is the Record
slides.body: Notes on building a verification pipeline, first pointed at the world, then at itself.
slides.source: post title; body = subtitle with the clause 'without quite meaning to' cut for length
slides.exec_caption: The label becomes permission: if the note says verified, build on it.

slides.label: The seed claim
slides.headline: Anthropic suspended two of its own models under U.S. export controls, then restored them weeks later.
slides.body: Dates, an agency, a resolution. Clean, falsifiable, and already sitting in front of me as a single, self-reported sentence.
slides.coda: That last part is the whole essay.
slides.source: post §intro, paras 1-2 (author's wording, 'of this year' and model names cut). Fact: anthropic.com/news/fable-mythos-access (directive Jun 12, 2026) and anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5 (controls lifted Jun 30; access restored per Jul 1 update), read 2026-11-10 Re-corroborated 2026-11-25 against both anthropic.com posts (all five facts supported).

slides.label: Mechanism and reason
slides.definition: after a reported jailbreak that got the model to identify software vulnerabilities.
slides.body: A claim that states the mechanism while omitting the reason is technically true in the way an alibi can be technically true.
slides.source: post §What the sources actually said, para 2 (body verbatim). Fact: anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5, read 2026-11-10: 'Amazon researchers had found a method of bypassing Fable 5's safeguards: prompting it so that it identified a number of software vulnerabilities' Re-corroborated 2026-11-25 against both anthropic.com posts (all five facts supported).

slides.label: One verb, two outcomes
list: Fable 5: back to users globally, with an improved safety classifier
Mythos 5: back to a set of U.S. organizations, under a separate government approval
slides.body: Completeness failures are the ones that pass every fact-check and still leave you with a wrong picture.
slides.source: post §What the sources actually said, paras 3-4. Fact: anthropic.com/news/redeploying-fable-5, read 2026-11-10: Fable 5 'to users globally on the Claude Platform, Claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork'; 'we trained an improved safety classifier'; Mythos 5 restored 'for a set of US organizations, following the US government's approval on June 26'. Post's 'vetted' and 'every surface' dropped: the primary source says neither Re-corroborated 2026-11-25 against both anthropic.com posts (all five facts supported).

slides.label: Then it found itself

rows.text: A named act and regulatory section, confirmed by outside analysis.
Read directly, that analysis framed the legal question as unresolved.
Fixing it quietly would have erased the only evidence that the check actually happened.

slides.coda: Verify before you build on it. That has to include the pipeline's own output.
slides.source: post §Then it found itself: row 01 = para 2 ('a named act, a named regulatory section, had been confirmed by outside analysis'); row 02 = para 4 (author's wording, compressed); row 03 = final para ('quietly fixing it and moving on — would have erased the only evidence that the check actually happened', compressed); coda = para 3 (author's wording). Row numbers are this slide's own, not the vault's. The pipeline's own history: the post is the authority. Replaces the 9-slide deck's slides 5, 6 and 8; slide 7 (frontmatter tangent) cut as a side lesson

slides.label: The gold in the seam
slides.callout: Pretending the break never happened would have cost more than showing it.
